summary: Learns hierarchical part/action/sequence-conditioned diffusion instead of test-time pose stitching.
method: CLIP action/part embeddings are PCA-reduced to 50 dimensions, expanded framewise and concatenated with noisy motion through an MLP; sequence and diffusion-step features are extra tokens. Unknown labels are zeroed; Beta-distributed random masking improves sparse-conditioning robustness.
conditions: Temporally aligned, potentially sparse sequence, action and seven-body-part text; FrankenStein extends existing mocap annotations using LLM reasoning.
evaluation: UniMotion, STMC and DART are adapted and retrained on FrankenStein using the same pose representation. Nine separate TMR-style evaluators assess seven parts, actions and sequences using R-Precision/M2T; realism uses FID/Diversity. Evaluations repeat 20 times with 95% confidence intervals. Annotation audit: 50 sequences, three experts.
limitations: Authors explicitly cannot generate minute-long sequences in one pass. Label audit samples only 50 sequences; learned semantic metrics do not establish contact physics. LLM-generated part annotations and adapted benchmark baselines need auditing; abstract promises release rather than proving current reproducibility.

limitations: Authors find Exp degrades for three/four text components as captions lack information. summary: Combines latent and text-attention energy formulations for concept conjunction and negation.

conditions: Multiple textual concepts, logical conjunction/negation; whole-motion latent representation rather than explicit per-frame body-part stitching.
evaluation: HumanML3D/KIT-ML evaluate ordinary text generation. MTT compares combined single text against multiple-text composition using original constituent captions. limitations: Appendix J reports failure on completely novel concepts. MTT semantic/transition metrics and synthetic augmentation do not demonstrate real object-contact consistency. Energy composition and text attention are empirical control mechanisms; neither supplies a physical feasibility certificate.

  abstract = 	 {Generating human videos with realistic and controllable motions is a challenging task. While existing methods can generate visually compelling videos, they lack separate control over four key video elements: foreground subject, background video, human trajectory, and action patterns. In this paper, we propose a decomposed human motion control and video generation framework that explicitly decouples motion from appearance, subject from background, and action from trajectory, enabling flexible mix-and-match composition of these elements. Concretely, we first build a ground-aware 3D world coordinate system and perform motion editing directly in the 3D space. Trajectory control is implemented by unprojecting edited 2D trajectories into 3D with focal-length calibration and coordinate transformation, followed by speed alignment and orientation adjustment; actions are supplied by a motion bank or generated via text-to-motion methods. Then, based on modern text-to-video diffusion transformer models, we inject the subject as tokens for full attention, concatenate the background along the channel dimension, and add motion (trajectory and action) control signals by addition. Such a design opens up the possibility for us to generate realistic videos of anyone doing anything anywhere. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets and real-world cases demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on both element-wise controllability and overall video quality.}
